title: Decode/extraction latency micro-optimization (LINUX-CPU)
scope: ffmpeg frame-extraction paths in tools/paddle-lab/detect_paddle.py (frame_iter windowed decode; decode_frames_at sparse exact-frame decode used by crop mode). No model, threshold, contract, or held-out changes. Held-out clips (wm-dink-01, afn-vic-rally1) untouched.

changes.what: decode_frames_at: input -ss seek at the first wanted frame's exact pts (plan_window_seek flooring arithmetic; select rebased to post-seek ordinals) + -frames:v early stop after the last wanted frame (previously the whole clip was decoded and drained regardless of the wanted set).
changes.proof: bench_decode.py --verify: every yielded frame sha256-equal to the direct full-clip decode frame at the same absolute index, on 4 cluster shapes per clip (early/mid-late/sparse-scattered/single-last-frame) on wm-volley-02 and afn-sasebo-rally1. 0 failures.

changes.what: frame_iter: replaced -fps_mode vfr with -vsync vfr (same semantics; -fps_mode exists only on ffmpeg >= 5.1). BUGFIX on Linux ffmpeg 4.4: any stride>1 or --decode-size invocation errored inside ffmpeg and frame_iter SILENTLY yielded zero frames.
changes.proof: test_timestamp_alignment.py green on both default clips (includes stride-3 window; every extracted frame byte-identical to direct full-clip CFR decode). E2E: default stride-1 window artifact frames byte-equal baseline vs fixed (25 frames, wm-volley-02 3750-4750ms).

changes.what: frame_iter + decode_frames_at now raise RuntimeError on nonzero ffmpeg exit instead of silently yielding a truncated/empty stream.
run_crops: fixed 4-value unpack of the 5-tuple ffprobe_meta (start_time added in C01) — crop mode crashed with ValueError before any decode on the integration base.
changes.proof: baseline: ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 4). Fixed: 2 frames / 3 crops processed on wm-volley-02 (cpu).

measurements.note: LINUX-CPU only. Decode-only wall clock (no inference), median of 7 runs per scenario, bench_decode.py. Clips: wm-volley-02 (1000x1080@25fps, 8.0s, 200 frames, single keyframe at frame 0) and afn-sasebo-rally1 (1920x1080@29.97fps, 4.4s, 132 frames, keyframes at 0 and 117). Never Mac/iPhone numbers.

beforeAfterMedianWallSec.scenario: frame_iter full clip stride1 (200 frames, unchanged path)
frame_iter mid window stride1 (74 frames, unchanged path)
frame_iter full clip stride1 (132 frames, unchanged path)
frame_iter mid window stride1 (73 frames, unchanged path)

measurements.contentDigests: bench digests (order-sensitive sha256 over per-frame sha256 + emitted indices/tMs) identical before vs after on every scenario that produced frames in both runs; the only digest changes are the two stride-3 scenarios that produced ZERO frames at baseline (Linux -fps_mode bug).
measurements.whyLateClusterGainIsSmall: wm-volley-02 has a single keyframe (frame 0) and rally1 only 0/117, so input seek still decodes from the previous keyframe; the measured win there comes from the -frames:v early stop. On clips with denser keyframes the seek term grows; no quality trade either way.
measurements.e2eSpotCheck: detect_paddle one-shot on wm-volley-02 3750-6710ms stride 3 (cpu): baseline 0 frames processed (silent), fixed 25 frames / 1114 paddle-proxy detections at 116ms/frame inference (LINUX-CPU).

gates.prettier: not applicable — only Python files touched (prettier has no python parser); repo TS untouched

notFabricated: No Mac/iPhone/cascade numbers claimed; all measurements above are LINUX-CPU decode-only or LINUX-CPU inference spot checks.
Held-out bundles wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 not read, benched, or referenced by the default bench clips.
afn-sasebo-rally2 bundle has no committed clip.mp4 on this base; it was not used.
